# S91 - Pega Blueprint (PDF) import through a reviewed transcription

A designer uploads a blueprint PDF; Orqix reads its page text, proposes a structured transcription with source page references, a person reviews and corrects every element, and only the reviewed transcription is converted into an ordinary draft. The draft then follows the same compiler gate, independent migration review, publication and execution as every other import. This implements the "supplied PDF" path of the [blueprint migration contract](../23-hackathon-requirements-baseline.md#10-blueprint-migration-contract).

**Honesty boundary.** One genuine Pega Blueprint export is in the repository: `examples/migration/pega-blueprint/RetailLoanOrigination.pdf` (an "Application Overview Document", Blueprint ID BP-63442, (c) 2024 Pegasystems, committed at the owner's request). `PegaBlueprintLayout` (`pega-blueprint` 0.1) is written against that one export; other export versions may lay pages out differently, so the report says which layout read the document and every element is still reviewed. Documents it does not recognise are read by the generic outline reader. The other fixtures are synthetic and labelled so.

## Pipeline

1. **Upload** (`POST /workspaces/{ws}/migrations/blueprints`, multipart `file` and optional `caseType`, `workflow.edit`). A Pega export can define several case types; one upload transcribes one: `caseType` names it (case and punctuation ignored), else the first. An unknown name is refused with 400 naming the case types the document has, and nothing is stored. Limits: 25 MiB, 60 pages, 1 MiB of extracted text. The first bytes must be `%PDF-`. The container multipart cap was raised to 25 MiB; `RequestLimitsFilter` still caps attachment uploads at 10 MiB + 64 KiB and this path at 25 MiB + 64 KiB, on `Content-Length` and on the stream. Encrypted PDFs (including an empty user password) and PDFs that forbid text extraction are refused with a clear message; damaged PDFs and non-PDFs are refused; a refused upload stores nothing.
2. **Page text** in the existing isolated extraction worker ([S29](S29-documents-integrations.md) `DocumentExtractionWorker`, separate JVM, 256 MiB heap for this mode, bounded concurrency, 60 s deadline, output bound). New worker mode `pdfpages` (protocol `ORQIX-PDF-PAGES/2`) writes one text block per page; control characters except line breaks and tabs are removed so a page cannot forge the separators. After each page's text it writes the page geometry: every text run the stripper wrote with its position, width, font size and bold flag, and every small filled shape (6 to 24 pt, at most 2,000 per page) with its bounding box and fill colour, which is how step icons are told apart. Geometry is bounded to 2 MiB per document; a document over that budget is returned without geometry (and is then read by the generic outline layout). The parent parses geometry strictly and rejects anything unexpected. Only `PDFTextStripper` and a path bounding-box pass run; nothing is rendered and images are not decoded: JavaScript, open actions, annotation actions, form actions and embedded files are never executed, opened or extracted. Their presence is detected (best effort) and reported as the info finding `BLUEPRINT_ACTIVE_CONTENT_IGNORED`. Image-only pages yield `BLUEPRINT_PAGE_WITHOUT_TEXT`; no OCR or image interpretation is attempted.
3. **Storage** (V150): the original PDF bytes and SHA-256 stay on `migration_job` (new source format `pegaBlueprint`; the source size check allows 25 MiB for this format only). `migration_blueprint_document` keeps page count, active-content flags, layout id/revision and (V204) the names of the case types the document defines but that were not transcribed; `migration_blueprint_page` keeps each page's text (for the Pega layout, its reading-order rendering, see below), SHA-256 and the number of unclassified lines; `migration_blueprint_transcription` keeps every saved transcription as an immutable revision with its canonical SHA-256, origin (`extracted`/`edited`), saver and time. The runtime role has `SELECT, INSERT` only on the new tables.
4. **Transcription** by a `BlueprintLayout` strategy, chosen per document (`BlueprintLayout.forPages`): `PegaBlueprintLayout` when every page has geometry, a section heading reads "Case Types" and a field-table header or a known step icon is present, otherwise `GenericOutlineLayout`.

   **`PegaBlueprintLayout` (`pega-blueprint` 0.1).** Font size and weight separate the export's parts: section headings (21 pt bold: "Case Types", "Personas", "Live Data", "Application Context"), item titles (17 pt bold: a case type, persona or data object), descriptions (15 pt), stage titles (13 pt) and step cards (12 pt) of the lifecycle grid, and the field table (13 pt bold header "Field Name / Description / Type / Primary"). Wrapped lines of one card, title or paragraph are joined. Each step card is assigned to the stage title above it in the same column, also when a column continues on the next page. The icon in front of a card gives the step kind: green user task -> `task`, blue check -> `approval`, yellow automation or notification -> `automated`, orange diamond -> a **decision**; another colour leaves the kind empty. One case type is transcribed: its stages, its steps and decisions in stage order (`next` and a decision's proposed `otherwise` follow that order; decisions get no conditions), and its fields (Text, Email, Phone, URL, Picklist -> string; Decimal, Currency, Percentage -> number; Integer; Boolean; Date; DateTime and anything else stay empty; the drawn "Primary" ticks are not read and nothing is marked required). Personas become roles; Live Data objects become integrations with the system of record named in "connects to ... as the system of record" as target. The export states no step roles, routes, rejection paths, SLAs or outcomes, so those stay empty and become findings. The layout also renders every page in reading order (lifecycle stage by stage with steps indented under their stage, table cells separated by tabs); that rendering is stored as the page text, so every element excerpt is highlighted in its page and the AI proposal reads the same order. Unclassified lines count lines of the rendering that belong to no transcribed element: the title page, the copyright notice and the case types that were not chosen.

   **`GenericOutlineLayout` (`generic-outline` 0.1).** It recognises section headings (Case type, Stages, Steps/Process steps/Assignments, Personas/Roles/Actors, Fields/Data/Data model, Decisions/Rules/Routing, SLAs/Service levels, Outcomes/Resolutions, Integrations/Systems) and the bulleted or numbered items under them, with simple `key: value` attributes (`role`, `stage`, `then`/`next`, `on reject`, `after`, `target`, ...), parenthetical types (`(approval)`, `(decimal, required)`, `(success)`), decision clauses `if <field> <op> <value> then <target>; otherwise <target>` and durations (`2 days`, `8 hours`, `3 business days`). Every element gets its source page, the source line as excerpt and disposition `proposed`. Values the text does not state stay empty. The only inferences are proposals a reviewer confirms: steps follow their listed order, a decision named `after: <step>` follows that step, and the last step leads to the single success outcome if exactly one exists. Text lines it does not attribute are counted per page and reported.
5. **Review and edit** (`GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{ws}/migrations/{id}/blueprint`). The transcription format `orqix-blueprint-transcription-0.1` is parsed strictly: allowed members, enums, lengths, unique ids and id/field-key patterns. Saving needs `expectedRevision` (409 when stale) and creates the next revision; a converted blueprint is frozen (409). Dispositions: `proposed`, `mapped` (reviewed against the source), `manuallyResolved`, `excluded` (needs a reason). The server, not the client, decides manual resolution: an element whose content differs from the extracted revision, or that the layout did not extract, cannot stay `mapped` and is stored as `manuallyResolved`.
6. **Findings** (`BlueprintFindings`) are recomputed on every save and stored as the job's compatibility report. Every element ends with a disposition: `BLUEPRINT_ELEMENT_MAPPED` (supported, with its target node after conversion), `BLUEPRINT_ELEMENT_EXCLUDED` (info, needs acknowledgement), or an open finding. Missing or ambiguous semantics are findings, never defaults: unreviewed element, step without role (blocker), undeclared role, unknown step type, unsupported step type (blocker), missing next/rejection route, route to an excluded element (blocker), decision without conditions (blocker), unknown condition field, value not fitting the field type, missing otherwise route, SLA without step/amount/unit, working-day SLA (blocker), SLA over 30 days, ambiguous SLAs, outcome without type, integration (blocker) and integration without target, field without type, more than 30 fields, no flow at all (`BLUEPRINT_NO_STRUCTURE`, blocker), no outcome (blocker), missing start, missing case type, invalid page reference, mapped element without page reference. Stages are informational (acknowledge). `BLUEPRINT_CASE_TYPES_NOT_TRANSCRIBED` (info) names the case types the document defines but that were not transcribed; upload again choosing one to migrate it as its own workflow. The report's first assumption names the layout that read the document.
7. **Optional AI structuring** (`POST .../blueprint/ai-proposal`, `workflow.edit`). Uses the S10 model profiles, price caps, budget and metering through `AgentModelPort` (prompt version `blueprint-transcription-v1`). Page texts are redacted (e-mail addresses, long digit runs, secret-like `key: value` pairs) and sent between `<page>` tags as untrusted data with instructions never to follow them. The answer must parse as a strict transcription; otherwise `AI_OUTPUT_INVALID` and nothing changes. Every element is forced back to `proposed`. The proposal is returned only; it is never stored or applied, and the reviewer may load it into the editor and save it like any edit. `AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` when AI is off. No database transaction is held while the model answers.
8. **Conversion** (`POST .../convert`, existing endpoint). The request must carry `transcriptionSha256` of the reviewed revision (409 when the transcription changed; the hash is part of the stored mappings, so the independent review binds it). `approvalRoutes`, `inputSchema` and the other mapping kinds are refused for a blueprint: routes and fields come from the transcription. All open blockers/actions must be resolved and info acknowledged. The admitted subset is converted to BPMN in memory and through the same `Analyzer`/`Converter` as XPDL, then the normal compiler gate in `DraftAuthoring` before any draft exists. Draft audit source `pega-blueprint-import`.
9. **Review, publish, run** exactly like other migrations: the migration-review state shows the mapper; an independent publisher approves and publishes; requests start and tasks are worked in the ordinary inbox.

## Exact supported subset

| Transcription element | Target |
|---|---|
| Step of type `approval` with a role | Approval step; the role id maps to a workspace group through the same explicit `groupMappings` as XPDL; approved goes to `next`, rejected to `onReject` (both required) |
| Decision with conditions on request fields | Exclusive branch: one comparison per condition (`>= > <= < == !=`; text and yes/no fields only `==`/`!=`; dates are not compared), converted by the same condition reader and branch semantics as a BPMN exclusive gateway, `otherwise` as default route. Overlapping conditions are the reviewer's responsibility |
| Field (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`) | Typed request field (`date` = string with `format: date`), required when stated; at most 30 |
| Outcome (`success`/`rejected`) | End with that business outcome and outcome kind |
| SLA in minutes, hours or days on an approval step | Approval due time (`dueAfterHours`, or `dueAfterMinutes` when not whole hours), elapsed time, at most 30 days |
| Role | Mapping key only; no source users, permissions or groups are created |
| Case type | Process id/name suggestion; the workflow key and name are chosen at conversion |
| Stage | Kept in the transcription; informational, not executed |

Not converted (reported, never dropped silently): manual tasks and automated steps (blocker until reconstructed and excluded with a reason), integrations (blocker; build an approved connection step later), working-day SLAs (needs a calendar mapping; blocker), parallel or inclusive routing, escalation actions, notifications, form layouts and screens, rule inheritance, data transforms, attachments, running cases, history and identities. Excluding an executable element is a scope change recorded with its reason and acknowledged at conversion; the reviewer then rebuilds it in the studio if needed.

## Security, permissions and audit

Same as the XPDL import (decision): upload, save, AI proposal and conversion need `workflow.edit`; reading the transcription needs `workflow.read`; other workspaces get 404. Publication keeps its own permission and the optional maker-checker policy. Page text is source data stored like the PDF itself. It is never written to logs or audit. Audit: `migration.uploaded` (migration id, source hash, adapter, page count, element count, transcription hash), `migration.blueprint.saved` (revision, transcription hash, element count, open findings), `migration.blueprint.ai.proposed` (profile, model, element count), `migration.converted`. The audit metadata allowlist enforces this. Prompts and answers are not stored or logged; AI usage is metered by tokens and cost only. Text inside the PDF is data: it cannot add sections, attributes, dispositions or mappings, and an instruction-like line is either unclassified or becomes an ordinary proposed element whose findings block it.

No new dependency: PDFBox was already used by the extraction worker. The synthetic sample generator uses only the Python standard library.

## UI

**Import workflow → Source format → Pega Blueprint (PDF)** uploads the file (25 MiB) with an optional **Case type** name (empty: the first). The job page shows the review screen instead of the generic mapping form: document facts and hashes, a mandatory-review notice, an alert for ignored active content, findings of the saved revision (status/alert regions), and every element as a card with editable fields and disposition next to the text of its source page with the source line highlighted. Buttons: mark unreviewed elements as reviewed, save, ask AI for a proposal and load it into the editor. The conversion form maps each used role to a workspace group, asks for the acknowledgements and converts the saved revision only (disabled while edits are unsaved). Mock mode refuses PDFs clearly; the real backend needs no mock.

## What remains

- `PegaBlueprintLayout` is written against one export. Collect more exports (other Pega versions, other industries, case types with child cases, processes, channels) and extend the layout and its fixtures; layout rules change only with a new revision.
- The export states no step roles, routes, rejection paths, outcomes or SLAs; reviewers add them. Check whether stages, case-type relationships, processes, data objects, personas and channels carry semantics the admitted subset can express; extend the subset only with equivalence evidence. Automated steps, decisions without conditions and integrations still block until excluded or reconstructed.
- Gear (automation) and bell (notification) icons share a colour and are both proposed as `automated`.
- Diagrams and images: OCR/vision interpretation remains optional and would feed proposals only, never conversions.
- Calendar-aware SLAs need a mapping to the workspace calendar ([section 6](../23-hackathon-requirements-baseline.md#6-calendar-aware-sla-and-overdue-behavior)).
- Genuine source acceptance (AC01) and business-owner sign-off stay required for any source-equivalence claim.

## Verification - 26 October 2026

Run in the `build/blueprint-pdf` worktree with JDK 21, PostgreSQL/Flowable through the backend test harness. Logs are local under `evidence/blueprint-pdf/` (ignored by Git).

- `PegaBlueprintApiTest` (6, real PostgreSQL/Flowable through the public API): upload the synthetic PDF (multipart) -> page texts and the committed expected transcription -> conversion refused while unreviewed and no workflow created -> stale revision 409 -> edit the SLA unit, exclude the integration with a reason, confirm the rest (revision 2; the edited SLA becomes `manuallyResolved`) -> stale hash 409, missing role mapping 422, `approvalRoutes` 400 -> convert (draft only, due times 48 h and 8 h) -> frozen transcription 409, idempotent replay, changed mappings 409 -> mapper cannot approve the migration review, a publisher approves and publishes -> 6,000 runs manager then finance to **Approved**, 4,999.99 runs manager only to **Approved**, a rejection ends **Rejected**; audit holds hashes and counts but no page text. Negative: damaged PDF, non-PDF, encrypted PDF, 61 pages (413), 25 MiB + 1 byte (413) all leave no job; JSON upload of `pegaBlueprint` 400; text without structure and injected instructions produce findings and no workflow; JavaScript and an embedded file are reported and ignored; AI proposal through the local OpenRouter stub is redacted, forced to `proposed`, not stored, and an invalid answer is `AI_OUTPUT_INVALID`; requester 403, outsider 404.
- `BlueprintPipelineTest` (7): real worker extraction, layout output equals `examples/migration/pega-blueprint/synthetic-blueprint.transcription.json`, findings, conversion, encrypted (password and empty password), damaged, non-PDF and 61-page refusals, active content ignored, strict parsing.
- `SecurityMatrixTest` covers the three new operations (foreign principals 404, no state change); `DocumentExtractionTest` unchanged and green.
- Full backend `mvnw.cmd clean verify -Dorqix.buildDirectory=target/verification -Dsurefire.useManifestOnlyJar=false`: BUILD SUCCESS, 524 and 910 tests in the two test phases, 0 failures, 4 skipped (pre-existing).
- Frontend: full Vitest suite 136 files / 969 tests pass (including `BlueprintReview.test.tsx`: upload, source-page display, AI-not-configured message, edit, save, role mapping, conversion request with `transcriptionSha256` and without routes; mock mode refuses PDFs). Typecheck, lint, production build, `api:check` pass; contract checks 88/88.

Not done: no run against a deployed Docker stack and no real-browser rehearsal of the new screen.
